amendments.made: 2026-10-04, after the first run on NBA data only (before any NHL/NFL/MLB demand data existed)
amendments.trigger: One NBA title-clinch event: the market resolved to 99.95%, so the odds-move size and odds level were far outside anything in training; the regression extrapolated to an absurd order and wiped out M3's result (-69% of opportunity, almost entirely from that one event).
amendments.change: (a) M3's odds features are clipped to the range seen in training (no extrapolation); (b) when the market has resolved (odds after the move >98% or <2%) M3 uses the class-only forecast, because a resolved market carries no magnitude information.
amendments.not_changed: event set, windows, demand proxy, economics, M0-M2, metrics, inference. Both the original-spec and amended results are reported.

amendments.made: 2026-10-04, during data QA of the NHL pipeline, before any NHL/NFL/MLB three-merchant result was computed
amendments.trigger: Clear game-driven moves were labelled 'off-court news' because the rule required the move to START during the game; in thinner markets (NHL) odds drift a little before puck drop and finish repricing hours after the final horn.
amendments.change: Signal classification (an input to M1-M3): a game explains a move if >=50% of the move happened inside [tip - 1h, tip + game length + 3h], using only prices up to the emission hour and only games that had finished before emission.
amendments.not_changed: detection thresholds, denoising gates, the scenario engine and its metrics.

prereg.title: Tipoff v2 - Three merchants: how much of a news event's opportunity does each kind of merchant capture?
prereg.written_before_results: 2026-10-04 (before scenarios.py was run on any league)
prereg.question: When a classified prediction-market signal fires at T=0, how much of the profit opportunity in the next 14 days does a merchant capture if they (0) do nothing special, (1) react with gut feel, (2) know the event's class statistics, (3) use Tipoff's quantified signal - versus (4) perfect hindsight?

event_set.include: every KEPT signal (passed all denoising gates) in every league-season
event_set.data_requirement: team's merch-search series has >=60% non-zero days in the season window; last-week sales rate R0 >= 1 index point; full window [-7, +13] inside the data
event_set.also_reported: REJECTED signals, to price what acting on noise would cost

decision.time: T=0 = the hour the signal is emitted; day 0 = that ET calendar day
decision.commitment: one order at T=0 covering days 0..13 (H=14), delivered instantly (execution latency ignored, per brief), no re-orders inside the window
decision.why_a_commitment: if stock could be refilled instantly every day, no forecast would ever matter and all merchants would tie; the commitment is what makes the size of the decision matter

demand.proxy: Google Trends daily merch-search index for the team (stitched regular-season pull), treated as proportional to unit sales
demand.R0: mean index over days -7..-1 (the merchant's last-week sales rate)
demand.X: sum of index over days 0..13 divided by R0 (demand in 'days of last week's sales')

merchants.M0_business_as_usual: orders 14 days at last week's rate times its usual buffer: Q = 14*exp(mu_all + z*sd_all), mu/sd of y over ALL team-days in training data (the best possible event-blind buffer)
merchants.M1_smart_gut_feel: knows the headline category only: good news / bad news (team still alive) / eliminated / won the title. Q = 14*exp(mu_cat + z*sd_cat) from training events
merchants.M2_pro_class_stats: strict benchmark: knows our full event class (clinch, win, loss, rival game, news...) and its historical average; classes with <5 training events fall back to the category. Q = 14*exp(mu_class + z*sd_class)
merchants.M3_tipoff: class + the market's quantification: OLS on training events, y ~ class effects + b*dlogit (size of the odds move) + c*logit(odds after the move); Q = 14*exp(yhat + z*sd_resid)
merchants.M4_hindsight: orders exactly the demand that arrived (upper bound)

prereg.profit: per event, in units of last-week daily sales: cu*min(Q,X) - co*max(Q-X,0); dollars = that * store's daily units

training.primary: within league, leave-one-season-out (train on the league's other season, test on this one)
training.secondary: pooled: train on every other league-season, test on this one

metrics.primary: opportunity captured = sum(profit_M - profit_M0) / sum(profit_M4 - profit_M0) over events
secondary: share of events where M3 >= M1
profit per event in $ for a 20-units/day store

hypotheses.H1: M3 (Tipoff) captures more opportunity than M1 (gut feel)
hypotheses.H2_strict: M3 captures more opportunity than M2 (class statistics without the market's magnitude)

inference.bootstrap: 2,000 resamples clustered by team-season (overlapping windows of one team are dependent); one-sided p = share of resamples where the difference <= 0
inference.placebo: 500 runs of M3 with the odds-move size shuffled among events of the same class; if M3's edge comes from the market's magnitude it must collapse
inference.noise: apply M3's sizing to REJECTED moves and compare with M0
